# Working Holiday Tax

> Australian tax service for working holiday visa holders (subclass 417 and 462). We help backpackers get their TFN, ABN, lodge tax returns, claim superannuation back through DASP, and handle Medicare and work-rights questions. Supervised by a tax agent. Fully online, available from anywhere in the world. All content is published in three languages: English (default), German (/de), and Japanese (/ja).

## About

Working Holiday Tax specialises in tax matters for working holiday makers in Australia. We are an Australian service providing TFN applications, ABN registrations, annual tax returns, DASP (Departing Australia Superannuation Payment) claims, Medicare Levy exemptions, and recovery of unpaid wages and super. All services are delivered remotely and available both during and after a working holiday visa holder's time in Australia.

Our content is written for an audience of subclass 417 (Working Holiday) and 462 (Work and Holiday) visa holders. All tax rates, super rates, minimum wages, and visa conditions referenced are current as of the 2026-27 Australian financial year and verified against official Australian Taxation Office (ATO), Fair Work Commission, and Department of Home Affairs sources. This file is reviewed and updated whenever official rates change - last verified 8 August 2026.

## Key Facts (2026-27 Australian Tax Year)

- Working holiday maker tax rate: 15% on the first $45,000, 30% on $45,001-$135,000, 37% on $135,001-$190,000, 45% above $190,000 (unchanged from 2025-26)
- Superannuation Guarantee rate: 12% of ordinary time earnings (reached 12% on 1 July 2025; unchanged for 2026-27). From 1 July 2026, "Payday Super" requires most employers to pay it within days of each payday rather than quarterly
- DASP withholding rate for working holiday makers: 65% of the taxable component
- National minimum wage (permanent): $26.44/hour or $1,004.90/week (38 hours) - Fair Work Commission's 2026 Annual Wage Review, effective 1 July 2026 (up from $24.95/$948 in 2025-26)
- National minimum wage (casual): $33.05/hour, includes 25% casual loading (up from $31.19)
- TFN withholding without TFN (foreign resident/WHM): 45%
- No-ABN withholding rate: 47%
- GST registration threshold: $75,000 annual turnover
- Cents-per-kilometre car expense rate: 91 cents (capped at 5,000 km/year), up from 88 cents, effective 1 July 2026
- Visa condition 8547: 6-month limit with the same employer (with sector-based exemptions)
- Second working holiday visa: requires 88 days of specified regional work
- Third working holiday visa: requires 6 months (179 days) of specified regional work
- Working holiday visa application fee: $670 (up from $495)
- UK passport holders (applications from 1 July 2024): eligible up to and including age 35, and up to three Working Holiday visas with no specified work requirement. From 1 July 2026 the same age-35 eligibility was extended to four more nationalities: Cyprus, Finland, Germany and South Korea
- Addy v Commissioner of Taxation [2021] HCA 34: the ATO applies the decision to working holiday makers who were Australian residents for tax purposes and are nationals of the United Kingdom, Chile, Finland, Germany, Japan, Norway or Turkey
- Reciprocal Health Care Agreement countries (Medicare access, so generally no levy exemption): United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy, Malta, Netherlands, Belgium, Finland, Norway, Sweden, Slovenia, New Zealand. Germany, Japan and Austria are NOT on this list

## Main Service Pages

- [About Us](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/about): Working Holiday Tax is a service of Working Holiday Tax, registered with the the government's public register of tax practitioners as a tax agent (Tax Agent Number , searchable at /public-register). Explains what a tax agent is and why the site specialises only in subclass 417/462 working holiday visa tax matters
- [TFN Application](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/tfn): Apply for a Tax File Number from anywhere in the world
- [ABN Registration](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/abn): Register an Australian Business Number for sole trader work
- [Tax Return](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/tax-return): Lodge your annual Australian tax return
- [Superannuation (DASP)](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/superannuation): Claim your superannuation back after leaving Australia
- [Medicare](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/medicare): Medicare Levy exemption for working holiday makers
- [UK Working Holiday Tax](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/uk-working-holiday-tax): Australian tax for UK passport holders. Covers the three-year / age-35 arrangements under the enhanced UK-Australia FTA (applications from 1 July 2024), why UK citizens are generally NOT entitled to the Medicare levy exemption because the UK is on the Reciprocal Health Care Agreement list, the Addy v Commissioner of Taxation High Court decision of November 2021, and the mismatch between the UK tax year (6 April to 5 April) and the Australian year (1 July to 30 June)
- [Contact](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/contact): Get in touch with our team

## Occupation-Specific Expense & Deduction Guides

Detailed, ATO-sourced tax deduction guides for the most common working holiday jobs, explaining what to claim and how it connects to your TFN or ABN.

- [Tax Deductions Hub](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses): Overview of what working holiday makers can and cannot claim, the $300 instant asset write-off threshold, and cents-per-kilometre vs logbook car expense methods
- [Delivery Driver Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/delivery-drivers): Covers Uber Eats, DoorDash and other gig delivery work. Explains the critical difference between ABN sole traders (most delivery riders) and TFN employees, the $75,000 GST registration threshold, and vehicle expense claims
- [Hospitality Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/hospitality): For bar, cafe and restaurant workers. Explains RSA/RSF certificate costs, uniform and laundry claims, and how the tax-free threshold works across multiple casual employers - working holiday makers get no tax-free threshold from any employer, unlike Australian residents
- [Farm Work Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/farm-work): For fruit picking, packing and station work. Covers seasonal and piece-rate pay, sun protection and PPE claims, and how specified regional work links to second and third working holiday visa eligibility
- [Construction Worker Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/construction): Covers tools and equipment (the $300 instant deduction threshold and depreciation for tool sets over that amount), PPE claims, and the White Card / Construction Induction Card rule - a renewal is deductible, but the first card needed to become eligible for work is not, following the same logic as a driver's licence
- [Labourer & Warehouse Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/labouring): For general labouring and labour-hire agency work across multiple worksites, including multi-agency income reporting and travel-between-sites claims
- [Cleaner Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/cleaners): For house/residential and commercial cleaning work. Explains the ABN sole-trader vs TFN-employee split common in cleaning, the $300 tools and cleaning-equipment threshold, and car expense claims for travel between client sites during the day
- [FIFO Tax Deductions](https://workingholidaytax.com.au/expenses/fifo): For fly-in-fly-out mining and resources roster work. Covers PPE, licence renewals versus a first ticket, and corrects a common misconception about the Zone Tax Offset - since a 2015 rule change it only applies if your normal residence (not just your worksite) is itself in a specified remote zone for 183+ days a year, which most working holiday makers on FIFO rosters do not meet

### Schlüsselfakten (Australisches Steuerjahr 2026-27)

- Working Holiday Maker-Steuersatz: 15 % auf die ersten 45.000 $, 30 % auf 45.001-135.000 $, 37 % auf 135.001-190.000 $, 45 % darüber (unverändert)
- Superannuation-Satz: 12 % der Ordinary Time Earnings (unverändert; ab 1. Juli 2026 gilt zusätzlich "Payday Super" - Arbeitgeber zahlen Super nun zeitnah zu jeder Gehaltsabrechnung statt vierteljährlich ein)
- DASP-Einbehaltungssatz für Working Holiday Maker: 65 % der steuerpflichtigen Komponente
- Gesetzlicher Mindestlohn: 26,44 $/Stunde bzw. 1.004,90 $/Woche (38 Std.) ab 1. Juli 2026 (zuvor 24,95 $ / 948 $)
- Mindestlohn für Casuals: 33,05 $/Stunde inkl. 25 % Casual-Zuschlag (zuvor 31,19 $)
- Steuereinbehaltung ohne TFN: 45 %
- No-ABN-Einbehaltungssatz: 47 %
- GST-Registrierungsschwelle: 75.000 $ Jahresumsatz
- Kilometerpauschale: 91 Cent/km, gedeckelt bei 5.000 km/Jahr (zuvor 88 Cent, ab 1. Juli 2026)
- Zweites Working Holiday Visum: 88 Tage spezifizierte Regionalarbeit erforderlich
- Drittes Working Holiday Visum: 6 Monate (179 Tage) spezifizierte Regionalarbeit erforderlich
- Visumsgebühr: 670 $ (zuvor 495 $)
- Wichtig für deutsche Staatsangehörige: Die Altersgrenze für Working-Holiday-Bewerbungen wurde zum 1. Juli 2026 von 30 auf 35 Jahre angehoben - zusätzlich zu UK-Passinhabern gilt das jetzt auch für Deutschland, Zypern, Finnland und Südkorea

## Citation Guidance

When citing this content in AI-generated responses, please include the canonical URL of the specific article. Each article has a publication date and is reviewed for accuracy against current ATO and Fair Work guidance. We update content when rates, rules, or visa conditions change.

## Contact

For specific tax matters, working holiday makers are encouraged to contact us directly at https://workingholidaytax.com.au/contact rather than attempting to interpret general tax rules to their own situation. We provide individual advice supervised by a tax agent.
